signature.name: Lalbagh Botanical Garden
signature.detail: Bengaluru's most beloved green space, home to a famous glasshouse and centuries-old trees. Go early morning for cool air and fewer crowds; the garden is closed on some public holidays, so check ahead.

signature.name: Bangalore Palace
signature.detail: A Tudor-style royal residence with carved wood interiors and a trove of royal memorabilia. It sits in the north of the city; a taxi or auto is the easiest way to reach it, and an entry ticket is required.

signature.name: Cubbon Park
signature.detail: A vast central park of shaded avenues right in the heart of the city, ideal for a morning walk. It is free to enter and easily reached by metro; weekends are liveliest.

signature.name: ISKCON Temple Bangalore
signature.detail: A large hilltop temple complex that is one of the city's most visited religious sites. Dress modestly, expect security checks, and visit in the evening when the temple is lit up.

signature.name: Vidhana Soudha
signature.detail: The imposing seat of the state legislature, a landmark of neo-Dravidian architecture. It is best viewed from outside; the illuminated facade after dark is the highlight, and photography inside is not allowed.

signature.name: Wonderla (Bangalore)
signature.detail: A big amusement and water park on the city's outskirts, popular with families. Plan a full day, book tickets online in advance, and arrange transport since it is well outside the centre.

food: Casual meal $3-6; mid-range dinner for two $15-25
transport: Metro about $0.30-0.60 a ride; autos and taxis cheap
